channel.title: Exploring Computer Science
channel.description: The CS theory behind the production code you write.

item.title: Overview
item.description: Beyond the fundamentals: how parsers and compilers actually work, what the OS scheduler decides for you, and the protocols and cryptography behind every API call.

item.title: Overview
item.description: The computer science foundations every working engineer should know cold — Big-O, type systems, recursion, trees, regex, and what actually happens when your code runs.

item.title: x86, ARM, and RISC-V
item.description: Why the same Dockerfile builds a different image on your M-series laptop than in CI, why AWS Graviton is cheaper, and why your phone doesn't need a fan. It's all one design decision, made decades apart.

item.title: How the OS Scheduler Actually Decides
item.description: Thousands of runnable threads, a handful of CPU cores. Something has to decide who runs next, for how long, and why a background job you `nice`d actually slowed down. Here's Linux's answer: the Completely Fair Scheduler.

item.title: Processes & Threads
item.description: Your 'concurrent' program on a single core isn't running things at the same time. It's switching between them thousands of times a second. Here's the unit that switch operates on, and what it costs.

item.title: Operating System Basics
item.description: Your code doesn't touch the disk, the network, or another process directly. It asks the kernel to, through a syscall. Here's the privilege boundary that makes that mandatory, not optional.

item.title: The Stack, the Heap, and Virtual Memory
item.description: Every process believes it owns all the RAM on the machine, in one continuous block starting at address zero. That belief is a lie the operating system tells for your own good — here's how, and why.

item.title: What Actually Happens When Your Code Runs
item.description: The CPU doesn't run Python, or Go, or anything you wrote. It runs one thing: machine code, one instruction at a time. Here's the fetch-decode-execute cycle underneath every program you've ever shipped.

item.title: Public-Key Cryptography: How Strangers Share Secrets
item.description: How do two machines agree on an encryption key while attackers watch every packet? The asymmetric crypto under TLS, SSH, and JWTs, minus the heavy math.

item.title: Anatomy of an HTTP Request and Response
item.description: Methods, status codes, headers, and body — the four parts of every HTTP exchange and how they form the contract your API actually promises.

item.title: Authentication vs Authorization in APIs
item.description: Who you are vs what you're allowed to do — and crucially, where each check happens. The conceptual model behind API keys, tokens, and sessions.

item.title: Client and Server: The Request/Response Lifecycle
item.description: Trace exactly what happens between a request and a response — who holds state, who does the work, and why the front-end/back-end split feels muddy.

item.title: Why HTTP APIs Forget You: Statelessness
item.description: HTTP APIs don't remember your last request. Learn why statelessness exists, what it costs, and how sessions vs tokens rebuild the memory you lost.

item.title: What an API Actually Is
item.description: An API is a contract, not a tool. Learn what an API really is, why it's a boundary between systems, and what you're invoking every time you curl.

item.title: Lists as Recursive Structures
item.description: Understand how CS theory defines a list recursively using cons and null, why recursive list operations are natural, and what Python lists, Clojure, and functional languages have in common.

item.title: Regular Expressions
item.description: The complete practical reference for writing and reading regex in production code — character classes, quantifiers, groups, flags, and common pitfalls.

item.title: Type Systems Basics
item.description: Understand type systems from a CS theory perspective — what types really are, how type notation works, and why every strongly-typed language enforces the same rules.

item.title: Big-O Notation
item.description: Understand Big-O notation for software engineers. Learn how to identify O(n²), O(n log n), O(n) complexities and optimize your code for production.

item.title: Compilers vs. Interpreters
item.description: Understand what compilers and interpreters actually do. The CS theory behind how source code becomes running programs, and why it matters for how you write and debug code.

item.title: Computational Thinking
item.description: Master the mental toolkit of computer science: Decomposition, Pattern Recognition, Abstraction, and Algorithm Design.
